## 2026-10-12 — Drew (Developer, money maths) — loanPricingDay: stopped loans priced at their stop (DONE, uncommitted)

**CEO call on open question 1:** a stopped loan is priced as of the earlier of today and `bill.ends_on`. This applies on the Loans page and on the View loan page.

- **API, in `src/lib/active-loans.ts`** (next to `loanFinished`): `loanPricingDay(bill: Pick<LoanBill, 'ends_on'>, today: string): string`. It returns `bill.ends_on` when that is before today, else today.
- **How to call it:**
  - Pass the day it returns to `loanStatus`, `loanHistory` and `upcomingPayments`.
  - Keep asking `loanFinished`/`loanEnding` with the real today.
  - `ends_on` is inclusive, as in `billWindow`, so a payment on the end date counts as made.
  - An end date on or after the last payment changes nothing. save_loan writes the last payment's date there, so a normal loan still reads as paid off.

**Migration `supabase/migrations/20261012100002_update_loan.sql`:**
- **Signature:** `update_loan(p_bill_id uuid, p_name, p_icon_id, p_principal, p_annual_rate, p_term_months, p_monthly_payment, p_total_interest, p_first_payment_on, p_funded_on, p_day_count_basis, p_card_id, p_bank_account_id, p_in_spending boolean, p_payment_day integer = null, p_payment_overrides jsonb = null, p_last_payment_on date = null, p_today date = null) returns bills`.
- **Security:** invoker, `search_path=public`, owner postgres. Revoked from public and anon, granted to authenticated (live ACL on the copy: postgres, authenticated, service_role, the same as save_loan). The bill row is locked `for update`.
- **Writes one transaction:**
  - Bill: name, amount = monthly payment, category 'loans', icon, recurrence 'monthly', next_due_on / starts_on / ends_on, card / account, in_spending (null leaves it as stored).
  - Loan: principal, rate, term, monthly payment, total interest, first payment, funded_on (null means a month before the first payment), basis (null means actual/365), overrides, payment_day.
  - Kept as stored: the bill id, created_at, brand, logo, note, the statement fields, charges and the reminder.
- **Refuses as save_loan does, in its words:**
  - P0001: term < 1; payment day outside 1–31; last payment outside the term (the term end is computed exactly as save_loan computes it).
  - The loans checks: overrides against the new term, rate 0–100, principal, basis.
  - bills_single_source.
- **New refusals:**
  - P0001 for a first payment of null.
  - P0001 "the card is not one of yours" / "the account is not one of yours". The foreign keys alone take anyone's card id.
  - P0002 "there is no such loan" for an unknown bill id, a bill with no loan, or another person's bill (RLS hides it). The loan is looked up before the sources are checked, so a missing loan reads as missing whatever else is sent.
- **Count floor** = greatest of:
  - (a) the local day the loan was added: `created_at` in the profile's timezone;
  - (b) the stored `starts_on`, only when it is later than the stored first payment;
  - (c) the 1st of the month after the last charge;
  - (d) the person's today, when the switch goes off → on.
  - Then `starts_on = greatest(first payment, floor)`.
  - `next_due_on` is the schedule's next payment on or after max(floor, today): the first payment, then the clamped payment day in the months after it, as `paymentDates`.
  - Nothing counts (floor > end): `starts_on` = the first payment and `next_due_on` null, as save_loan's deviation 3.
  - Every counted payment is ≤ today: anchored on the last payment, so a payment due since the recorders last ran is still written. The sweep then rolls it past `ends_on`, and the reminders ignore it (A's fix).
- **Deviation from the brief, for Dmitri:** the brief says never before the stored `starts_on`. Taken literally, that is wrong for a loan added before its first payment. There `starts_on` is just the first payment, not a floor.
  - Example: added 12 Oct with the first payment on 27 Nov, then edited on 20 Oct to 27 Oct. The literal rule would never count the 27 Oct payment, even though it is still to come.
  - It would also back-fill a loan saved already paid off (starts_on = its 2019 first payment).
  - (a) + (b) is the F1 floor itself. (b) keeps every floor set since: save_loan's count floor, a switch back on, a floor after a charge.
  - The M2 client guard on the bill-form path keeps the literal rule. After P2's routing a loan never reaches that form, so I left it.

## 2026-10-12 — Dmitri (Development Lead) — Add Loan P2 review: GO, no MUST. Migration B is READY for the Founder's go, after the read-only live checks below. Read-only.

**Gates:** tsc 0; eslint (cache cleared, `--no-cache`, `--max-warnings 0`, src) 0 errors, plus the old setup.test.tsx warning; prettier clean on all 45 changed TS files; full jest 332/332 suites, 7,097 tests. The v57 router docs and types export `Redirect` and `useIsFocused`.

**Migration B (`20261012100002_update_loan.sql`):**
- **It touches no existing row.** It adds one new function and nothing else. Running it twice is safe (create or replace, revoke, grant).
- **Security:** security invoker with `search_path=public`. Revoked from public and anon, granted to authenticated.
- **RLS:** bills and loans have `for all` own-row policies, so the caller's updates are allowed and limited to their own rows. Someone else's bill reads as P0002. Card and account ownership is checked through RLS-visible existence.
- **Refusals leave nothing half-written.** Every raise comes before the writes. A failing loans check (the changed payments against the new term, or the payment day) aborts the call and rolls back the bill update with it.
- **Triggers:** bills and loans carry only their updated_at triggers.

**Live checks wanted before the push (read-only):**
- No `update_loan` exists live (`pg_proc` by name).
- The migration history ends at 20261012100001.
- `pg_policies` for bills, loans, cards, bank_accounts, charges and profiles match the files: own-row policies, and bills/loans `for all`.
- The triggers on bills and loans are only `*_set_updated_at`.
- `bills.in_spending` and `loans.payment_day` exist.

**Decisions:**
- **Diego's floor deviation: accepted.** The literal "never before the stored starts_on" rule is wrong in two cases. For a loan added before its first payment, starts_on is not a floor. For a loan saved already paid off, it would back-fill.
  - (a) the add day plus (b) a stored starts_on later than the first payment is F1 itself.
  - (c) the month after the last charge keeps to one charge per cycle.
  - (d) a switch turned back on counts from today.
- **Q2, both parts: agreed.** Payments moved to after the add day but before today count, as if the loan had been saved that way. Lengthening a finished loan counts from its last charge on. Both follow F1, and wrapped-up months stay frozen (R7).

**Checked:**
- **No redirect loop.** `/loan/[id]` sends a bill with no loan to `/bill/[id]`, and `/bill/[id]` sends on only when the read found a loan. Both use the same query key, so one read decides both. A failed read shows the bill.
- **Old bills and subscriptions still open their own pages.** An old manual Loans bill goes from `/loan/[id]` to its bill page and edits in Add bill.
- **Navigation:**
  - An edit save goes back to `/loan/[id]`.
  - Delete makes one `finishFlowOn('/loans')`. The loan page beneath does not pop itself while it is not focused, and the edit page keeps the last-read loan.
  - Push taps on `/bill` land on the loan page.
- **Cent-exact:**
  - The card, upcoming and history rows all come from the `amortise` rows on `loanTermsForBill`, the same schedule the Loans page reads.
  - `loanScheduleParams` carries `day`.
  - By hand on the wireframe loan: 27 Oct is $54.83 interest + $369.97 principal, and 27 Sep is $58.60 + $366.20.
  - Stopped loans are priced as of their stop on both pages through the shared `loanEnding`.
- **en/es/fr:** complete, and every loan, loanFlow and toast.loan key is used. The delete wording is accurate: charges, the loans row and the reminder all cascade.
- **Comment style:** fine.
- **Tests:** meaningful (B's 52 SQL checks with 7 mutants caught; loan-view's sweep across 13 loans; the redirect and focus cases).

**Nice-to-haves:**
1. History "See all" draws every made payment at once, with no virtualising. Check a 30-year loan late in its term on the 13 Pro Max.
2. `p_today` comes from the device. A wrong clock moves the switch-on floor. Clamp it to within a day of the profile's day.

**Outcome:** Done. Nothing committed. Every payoff figure matches an independent Python reference (exact fractions, own calendar) row by row. Loans without payoffs are unchanged to the cent.

**Rules as built:**
- **Interest first (F2), full and partial:**
  - On the payoff day, the interest built up since the last payment or payoff posts, rounded half up once on the exact BigInt path.
  - The payoff pays that interest first, then principal.
  - Interest it does not cover (a payoff smaller than the interest) is paid first by the next payment. It is not added to the balance.
- **Full payoff:** the schedule ends that day, with no row after it. `payoffOn` and `loanStatus.lastPaymentOn` are the payoff day.
- **Partial payoff:** the stored monthly payment stays, later periods accrue on the smaller balance, and the last payment takes up the gap. Several partials are allowed.
- **Same day:**
  - A payoff on a due date posts after that day's payment.
  - Payoffs on the same day post in the order they were recorded.
- **Day count:** the loan's own basis. Monthly rests are per diem on actual/365 on both sides of a payoff, matching the existing quote rule. 30/360 counts pieces in thirtieths, so a payoff on the 31st charges 4 + 27 days that period.
- **Contract:** payoffs are part of it. `scheduleWithOverrides` keeps them. `solvePayment` ignores them, so the level payment never moves. The typed monthly-payment floor is judged on the loan as lent; otherwise a clearing payoff would let any payment through.
- **checkPayoff:**
  - Before the start: refused.
  - After today: refused.
  - More than the quote: refused, with the quote.
  - A full payoff before the last payment made, or before a payoff already recorded: refused.
  - A back-dated partial that would cut a later payoff, or end the loan before a payment already made: refused, with the most that can be paid that day, found by bisection.
- **CEO change, mid-task (Dana's hand-back):** a full payoff is now allowed ON a payment day. That day's payment posts first and the quote is the balance it leaves, so payoffDays.earliestFull is the last payment's own day.
  - Proof: $424.80 + $10,303.70 = $10,673.67 + the period's $54.83, so the money is the same either way.
  - `ends_on` = that day is inclusive, so the instalment is recorded once and nothing after it is charged.
  - Diego's `record_loan_payoff` now uses `charged_on > p_paid_on` and "the first payment strictly after", which is equivalent.

  - On 26 Oct: $10,726.67 (29 days, $53.00).

**Migration `supabase/migrations/20261012100003_loan_payoffs.sql`:**
- **Table `loan_payoffs`:**
  - Columns: id, user_id (default auth.uid()), bill_id, paid_on, amount numeric(14,2) > 0, kind full|partial, card_id / bank_account_id (on delete set null, at most one of them), counted, bill_ends_on_before, bill_next_due_on_before, created_at.
  - `bill_id` references `loans(bill_id)` on delete cascade. The app knows a loan by its bill, and the payoff goes with its loan.
  - RLS: own rows, for all commands.
  - A unique partial index allows one full payoff per loan. Indexes on (bill_id, paid_on) and (user_id, paid_on).
  - Trigger `loan_payoffs_own_rows`: only your own loan, card and account (as receipt_books).
  - Published for realtime (replica identity full). The app does not listen to it (see Fallbacks).
- **`record_loan_payoff(p_bill_id, p_paid_on, p_amount, p_kind, p_card_id, p_bank_account_id, p_last_payment_on = null, p_today = null)` returns `loan_payoffs`:**
  - Security invoker, `search_path=public`, revoked from public and anon, granted to authenticated.
  - Locks the bill. Every refusal comes before any write.
  - Today: p_today, else the profile's timezone, as update_loan.
  - Start: funded_on, else the first payment less a month.
  - A full payoff (R5): no charge dated after it, no payoff dated after it, and no scheduled payment after its day up to today (first payment, then the clamped payment day). The payment day itself is allowed (CEO/Drew): that day's instalment counts once and `ends_on` is inclusive.
  - `counted` = the bill's in_spending at that moment.
  - Bill:
    - A full payoff sets `ends_on` = paid_on.
    - A partial one sets `ends_on` = p_last_payment_on (within the term and ≥ paid_on), or keeps it when that is null.
    - An end before the bill's count floor stops the bill instead: next_due_on null, and ends_on stays on starts_on (bills_period_order).
    - Lowering the floor was rejected: mutant m04 showed the recorder then writes a phantom instalment on the payoff day (first payment 27 Nov, paid 27 Oct).
  - It always writes the bill, so other phones hear of it through the bills feed.
- **`delete_loan_payoff(p_id, p_last_payment_on = null)` returns boolean:**
  - False for a payoff already gone or not yours.
  - Locks the bill, then the payoff.
  - Only the latest payoff (paid_on, created_at, id) can be removed (CEO F3).
  - A full payoff: `ends_on` = p_last_payment_on, else the stored `bill_ends_on_before`. A bill that payoff stopped runs again from the next due date it took.
  - A partial payoff with a last payment: `ends_on` = that date.
  - A partial payoff with null: the bill stays exactly as it is (Dana's stopped-early case). It is still written.
- **`update_loan` recreated:** same 18 arguments, grants and invoker. One block is added:
  - With a full payoff on file, `ends_on = least(contract end, paid_on)`, or stopped when that comes before the floor.
  - The contract's end (and its next date, when stopped) goes to the payoff, so removing it puts back the edited loan.

  - `type StopBillValues = { ends_on: string } | { starts_on: string; ends_on: string; next_due_on: null }`
  - `billStopped(bill: StoppableBill, today: string): boolean`: true when there is no next date, or `ends_on <= today`. It is the same rule as `loanBillEnded`, and a test pins that they agree.
  - `stopBillValues(bill: StoppableBill, today: string): StopBillValues`:
    - an end already on or before today is kept, never moved later;

- **CSV:**
  - BOM, CRLF and RFC 4180 quoting.
  - Formula guard: a leading `= + - @`, the same after leading spaces, their full-width forms, or a tab/CR/LF gets a `'` prefix. The amount column is built from cents, so it is never guarded.
  - `plainAmount` uses `wholeCents ?? toCents`. `toCents` keeps only 12 significant digits, so on its own it writes $999,999,999,999.99 as 1000000000000.00.
- **PDF HTML:**
  - Rendered through WebKit (the macOS print path, the same engine as iOS) and Chrome, on A4 and Letter.
  - A table failed in WebKit: it does not repeat `thead`, and it ignores break avoidance on `tr`/`tbody`, so a month heading was left alone at the foot of a page.
  - Now built from blocks: rows never split, a month heading always stays with its first row, and the column headings print once.
  - Light only, the system font, accent `#905479` heading and rule. Month totals and the grand total come from `sumMoney`.
- **`exportHref`:** a query string cast `as Href` (the push.ts pattern). Metro has since registered `/payment-export`.

## 2026-10-12 — Dilip — Bills/subs pages P11: share an export, plus the R2 timing. DONE (no commits).
**Outcome:**
- `sharePayments` writes the CSV, or prints the PDF, into its own cache folder under `exportFileName` and opens the share sheet.
- The native modules load only inside the call.
- A missing module, a refused share or a failed write gives the one failure line. A cancel is not a failure.
- R2: the 7-year payments chain is about 40–90 ms in node, and about 3× less with a payments-only ledger.

**Files:** `src/api/payment-export.ts` and `src/__tests__/payments/payment-export-api.test.ts` (42 tests).

**API:**
- `sharePayments(request: ShareRequest): Promise<ShareResult>`.
  - `ShareRequest = { kind, year, dialogTitle } & ({ format: 'csv'; csv } | { format: 'pdf'; html })`.
  - `ShareResult = { status: 'done' } | { status: 'failed'; error }`.
- `pdfPage(region)`, `LETTER`, `A4`.

**Behaviour (checked against the v57 docs and the installed native code):**
- **Loading:** `expo-file-system`, `expo-sharing` and `expo-print` are `require`d inside the call, never at import. expo-print's entry calls `requireNativeModule` as it loads, so an import would crash today's dev clients. A dev client without expo-print still shares a CSV.
- **Files:** they go to `Caches/payment-exports/`, which is cleared before each export (best-effort), so only the newest export is kept. Nothing else in the cache is touched.
- **PDF:**
  - expo-print writes `Caches/Print/<UUID>.pdf`. That file is moved, not copied, so it never piles up, and it is deleted if the move fails.
  - Paper: Letter in CLDR's Letter regions (BZ CA CL CO CR GT MX NI PA PH PR SV US VE, read from the system ICU), A4 elsewhere. The region comes from `getLocales()[0].regionCode`. `PDF_MARGINS` are passed to the print call.
- **Share:** iOS `shareAsync` (57.0.14) resolves on every dismissal, so a share and a cancel are the same `done`. It rejects only for an unreadable file or no view controller, and that becomes the one failure line, with the cause sent to `failureMessage`. `isAvailableAsync()` false is also a failure, before anything is written. The installed iOS code ignores `UTI` (passed anyway, it is correct for Android).

**R2: synthetic 7-year account.**
- **The account:** 18 bills (14 monthly, 2 weekly, quarterly, yearly), 16 subscriptions, 3,143 charges, 10,232 receipts, 365 pay rows and 2 payoffs. The ledger has 13,299 entries, of which 3,037 are payments.
- **The machine:** Intel i9-9980HK, slower per core than the A15.
- **Median ms (with JIT / interpreter only, `--jitless`, which stands in for Hermes):**

  | Step | JIT | Interpreter only |
  |---|---|---|
  | Full 7-year `ledgerEntries` | 28–33 | 53–56 |
  | Same ledger without receipts, salaries and pay | 8.9 | 17.4 |
  | `paymentEntries` | 3.6 | 6.3 |
  | Years and month groups (`yearSummary` ×2, `yearsList`, `monthGroups`) | 10–11 | 15 |
  | Month window `ledgerEntries` | 3.2 | 6.1 |
  | `planMonth` | 1.6–2.6 | 2.8 |
  | Building an all-years CSV and HTML (135 KB and 568 KB) | 37 | 55 |

- The payments-only ledger gives identical bill and subscription entries and identical `paymentEntries`. That is checked on the fixture and in the source: receipts, pay and salaries are separate loops.
- **For Diego (P10):**
  - Feed `ledgerEntries` empty receipts, salaries and pay for the payment pages: about 3× less work.
  - `useMemo` is per page, so every payment page re-walks 7 years on mount. A module-level memo keyed by the queries' data identity makes it once per data change.
- **On the phone:** confirm on the Release build.

**Gates:**
- tsc: 0 errors in my files. The 4 others are in Diego's in-progress `payment-filters.test.tsx`.
- eslint (cache cleared, `--no-cache`, `--max-warnings 0`): 0.
- prettier: clean.
- jest: my 4 suites plus the guards, 9 suites and 118 tests, green.
- 13 API mutants, all caught (includes a top-level import of expo-print and of expo-file-system).

**Open:**
1. **P18:** iOS cannot tell a share from a cancel, so there should be no success toast (the sheet is its own confirmation). The page should also hold its busy state until the call returns, because a second sheet cannot open over the first.
2. **CEO:** the R2 mitigations above sit in Diego's P10.

The cross-check holds in every month from Jan 2020 to Oct 2026: the month page's figure plus that month's payoffs equals history's month total, to the cent, on both tabs. The demo seed was recomputed two independent ways, and the two agree.

**Files (new):**
- `src/lib/payment-years.ts`

**P1 follow-ups** (in `bill-month.test.ts`, now 56 tests):

**API:** as in plan §1.3, plus exported types `Paid`, `YearSummary`, `MonthGroup<T>` and `YearsList`. One change: `yearsList().first` is `number`, not `number | null`. It is always the oldest year listed, which is this year on an empty account ("Paid since 2026").

**Rules:**
- **Average:** the year total ÷ months, rounded half away from zero on whole cents. The months run from January, or from the first payment's month when that falls in the year, to this month (or December for a past year). A year before the first payment has 0 months and a $0.00 average.
- **Month groups:** a group's `count` and `total` cover the whole month; its `rows` start at `listFloor`.
- **Seven calendar years:** rows before `paymentFloor(today)` or after today are ignored everywhere.

**Cross-check fixture:** seven years, swept to today. It covers:
- a rent rise and a moved due day;
- weekly, quarterly, yearly and set-period bills;
- a stopped bill;
- a loan paid off in full and one in part;
- a flag-off loan with a counted payoff and an uncounted one;
- a cancelled subscription and a renamed plan;
- a plan that was never recorded.

Before the sweep, the only gap is exactly what the sweep owes: Sep +$554.00 (bills) and +$4.50 (subscriptions), Oct +$1,335.00. After the sweep the gap is gone and the month page has not moved.

**Demo seed** (scratchpad only, read from `supabase/seed/demo-sam.sql`, never the live DB). It was recomputed in Python with its own date stepping, and separately through the app's recorder, ledger and `paymentEntries`. The two agree. ## 2026-10-12 — Diego — Bills/subs pages P10: `usePayments` + `usePlanMonth` (DONE, no commits)
**Outcome:** both hooks are built on `ledgerEntries` itself, given only bills, subscriptions, charges and payoffs. They make one shared walk per data change, whichever page asks. The bill/subscription entries, the payments, the month views, the free floor and the hidden-history answer are each proven equal to `useLedger`'s on one rich account.

**Files (new only):**
- `src/api/payment-ledger.ts`
- `src/__tests__/payments/payment-ledger.test.tsx` (58 tests)

**API:**
- `usePayments(today): PaymentsData`. It returns `{ payments: readonly PaymentEntry[], listFloor, free, labelOf, sources, isLoading, isError, refetch }`.
  - `payments` covers `paymentFloor(today)`..today, newest first, frozen.
  - `listFloor` is `useLedger`'s own floor (`historyFloor(!useKnownFree())`), held to the window's start. That gives 15 Jul on free, and 1 Jan 2020 on Pro and while Pro is unknown.
  - tsc checks that it fits Dilip's `UseExportPayments`.
- `usePlanMonth(kind, month, today): PlanMonthData`. It returns `{ view, hasPlans, labelOf, isLoading, isError, refetch }`, exactly Dana's `PlanMonthData` (tsc checks it against `UsePlanMonth`, and a test checks the keys). It takes `today` as its third argument, as her seam does.
- `planLedger(reads, range, today)` (pure) and the type `PlanReads`.

**Decisions:**
- **No receipts, salaries or pay.** The hooks never read them; a test counts the reads at 0. The `useLedger` kept-years clamp is applied as-is (`historyFloor(true)`).
- **Memo:** a module-level WeakMap chain, keyed by the identities of the bills, subscriptions, charges and payoffs data. The last key is user | window | today, plus kind | month for the month view.
  - Data the query cache drops takes its answers with it.
  - At most 16 answers are kept per data set (first in, first out).
- **Partial data:** nothing is worked out while any of the 4 plan reads has no data. The page shows loading or error then, and the reads arriving one by one would otherwise each walk 7 years.
- **isError / isLoading:** bills, subscriptions, charges, payoffs, cards and accounts. `refetch` re-reads all six.
- **`hasPlans`:** any bill that `countsInSpending`, or any subscription, or anything the view draws. A kept-out loan with a charge that month is not hidden.

**Proofs:**
- Equal to `useLedger`: 8 windows (pure), the payments hook, and 9 months × 2 kinds, including Oct 2019 across the kept floor.
- October bills: $2,397.55 · 8 · 3 · 5 · Next Cleaner 15 Oct, with the phone due today filled.
- Walks:
  - 4 pages open: 1 walk.
  - A new charge, a new payoff, or a new day (same year, and New Year): exactly 1 walk each, and every page gets the new array.
  - A refetch that brings unchanged data, or a free/Pro flip: 0 walks.
- Accounts: one account's rows never appear in another's render. A second account seeded with the first's very data objects is still worked out afresh.

## 2026-10-12 — Drew — `bill-month` payoffs on the card (`extras`), per the Founder's decision: DONE (no commits)
**Outcome:** the card keeps its due figure. `PlanMonth.extras` now carries the month's loan payoffs, and the line "+ $X extra on … · $Y in all" can be drawn from it. In every month of the seven-year fixture (2020-01 to 2026-12), the due figure plus the extras equals Home's Monthly bills tile to the cent.

**Type:**
```ts
export type MonthExtras = {
  total: number;  // payoffs in the month, whole cents
  count: number;  // payoffs
  loans: number;  // distinct loans
  name: string | null;  // the loan's name when every payoff is on one loan
  inAll: number;  // PlanMonth.total + total, whole cents (Home's tile)
};
PlanMonth.extras?: MonthExtras | null;
```
- It is null when the month has no payoff, and always null for subscriptions.
- `planMonth` always sets it. It is declared optional only because Dana's `plan-month-parts.test.tsx` builds two `PlanMonth`s by hand without it (lines 195 and 246), and a required field breaks tsc there. It can be made required once those two literals add `extras: null`.
- Payoffs still never count in the total, n, p, c or Coming up.
- A payoff counts whatever its loan's flag is. One made while the loan did not count is not in the ledger, as on Home.
- Only payoffs dated in the month count, whatever window `entries` covers.

**Tests:**
- `bill-month.test.ts`, now 64:
  - one loan ($2,884.00 in all);
  - two loans, one of them kept out of monthly bills ($1,500.00, 2 loans, $3,384.00);
  - two payoffs on one loan;
  - an uncounted payoff;
  - a month with nothing due;
  - Subscriptions;
  - a wide entries window.
- `payment-cross-check.test.ts`, now 10:
  - Home's tile, built exactly as home.tsx builds it: `rangeFor('month')`, `kind === 'bill'`, the sum of `Math.abs`. It equals the card's due + extras in every month from 2020-01 to 2026-12. Extras fall in 2024-03 (a loan now kept out of bills), 2025-09 (partial), 2025-11 (two loans) and 2026-02 (full).
  - A separate account with a payoff in a month where nothing is due.
  - History's month totals now also check `extras.total` in past months.

- eslint (cache cleared, `--no-cache`, `--max-warnings 0`) and prettier are clean on my 5 files.

## 2026-10-13 — Diego — Part 5 investigation: "Something went wrong" causes, double-filing, speed, Sentry (READ-ONLY, no src edits)
**Outcome:** the habit failure in screenshot 5 was the database's own Pro wall refusing an account the server has never seen as Pro. It is our code, not a Supabase fault. It is also not a few seconds of webhook lag: that account has no entitlements row at all, 11 hours later.

**Habit case (live DB, read-only `db query --linked`):**
- The screenshot account is NOT Sam. It is c2ad25b3-df47-406d-919c-dae33013a164: card "Sam" (#161616) and bank ACCOUNT "Hh" (nickname Hh, bank Cuff, #FA8F6F). "Hh" is an account, not a card.
- That account has no `entitlements` row at all, so `is_pro()` is false now and always was.
- Its sign-in was at 2026-10-13 04:10:57 UTC, and a bill was saved at 04:27:49 UTC. The screenshot reads 12:23, which is 00:23 EDT = 04:23 UTC.
- The previous account, 95810acb, holds the sandbox monthly subscription. Its last webhook write was at 04:13:22 UTC (expires 04:18:38) and nothing came after it, not even an EXPIRATION.
- Sam (bdb18bea) has pro=true, product `dev.pro-state-script`, expires null, written 2026-10-09 by the seed script. `is_pro` is true for Sam, so Sam can never hit this wall.
- The app thought c2ad25b3 was Pro: `useProGate` only shows the form when pro && ready, and Release has no override. So RevenueCat's SDK said Pro for an account the server never heard about.
- Proven code fact: RevenueCat TRANSFER events carry no `app_user_id` (RC docs: TRANSFER uses only `transferred_from`/`transferred_to`). The webhook skips them (index.ts:39-45). A subscription that moves to a second account on the same Apple ID (sign in to another account, Restore, or a sandbox renewal posted under the new id) never reaches the server.
- Second factor: sandbox expiry plus a stale SDK cache gives the same "app says Pro, DB says no".
- To confirm: RC customer history for c2ad25b3 (look for "Transferred"), the RC webhook log, the edge log line "skipping non-uuid app_user_id TRANSFER", and the Sentry event "Tracking spending habits is part of Skip Pro." at about 04:23 UTC.

**Other findings (full list in my report to the CEO):**
- Background refetch errors blank Home's lists and figures even with good cached data (`anyError`, queries.ts:111/1167, which is month-end's file).
- Not-ready past-choice reads show the failure line in 10 places.
- A scan that reads nothing shows the failure line (add-receipt.tsx:758).
- Partial-step double-files: add-subscription, add-card, add-account and salary have no written-id guard.
- Dropped-response double-files: every `useCreate` insert, `useCreateHabit`, `save_loan`, `record_loan_payoff` (partial), payments, goals and pots.
- Every direct-insert table accepts a client id (checked live), so the client-id fix for direct inserts needs no migration.

**Speed:**
- The DB is not the bottleneck. App queries average 1-25 ms on the server, and indexes cover the RLS and order filters.
- The costs are on the client: about 14 parallel reads on Home, a refetch of every mounted query on each resume after 30 s, about 10 serial sweep round trips, realtime echoes that re-read after our own writes, and an unconditional timezone UPDATE each launch (803 calls).
- PostgREST schema-cache reloads (1,252 since 26 Aug; `pg_timezone_names` mean 572 ms, max 3.5 s) come from our DDL.

**Gates:**
- I changed no src files.
- jest on the 8 related suites: 92/92.
- tsc is not clean, from other sessions' in-flight files (add-loan-form.test.ts, then insights.tsx), none of them mine.

## 2026-10-13 — Dana — Logic fixes Part 4: after buying Pro, straight into the feature (DONE, no commits)
**Outcome:** the explainer is never shown to someone with Pro. Buying on `/pro`, Restore on `/pro` (when an explainer opened it), and buying or restoring on `/pro-offer` all end inside the feature the person was opening. Mid-task gates return to their filled page. `/pro` from Settings behaves as before.

**How it works:**
- `src/app/pro-feature.tsx` takes `?next=`. It uses expo-router 57's `useFocusEffect` (a fork that waits for navigation, made for redirects), fires once, and only while on top.
- Once Pro, it goes to:
  - a valid in-app `next`;
  - else `router.back()`;
  - else (a cold link, nothing beneath) the feature's own page;
  - else `/home`.
- It draws nothing while Pro is unknown or true, so a payer arriving by link never sees the price.
- "Get Skip Pro" pushes `/pro?from=feature`. "Not now" uses `goBack()`, so a cold link is not a dead button.
- `src/lib/pro-next.ts` (new): `inAppNext` keeps only `/path` values. expo-router sends `https:` and `//host` to Safari.

## 2026-10-13 — Drew — Add loan: a First payment date replaces the payment-day chips (Part 2+3) (DONE, no commits)
**Outcome:** the details page has a **First payment** date field (the same `DateBox` + inline calendar as Start date). A 30 Nov 2025 start can now take its real 14 Jan 2026 first payment, and Review prices it as the Founder's real statement, to the cent. No engine change, no migration.

**Behaviour:**
- Default: a month after the start on the start's day, clamped (`defaultFirstPayment`); 31 Jan → 28 Feb, still paid on the 31st. Under it, one muted line: "Then every month on the 14th" (`dayOrdinal`: 14th / día 14 / le 14, 1er), "…on the 30th, or the last day in shorter months" for 29/30, "Then on the last day of every month" for 31.
- An untouched first payment moves with the start date; a picked one stays. If the start moves onto or past it, a hint in TextField's error style, "Pick a first payment after the start date.", replaces the line. Continue says the same words.
- **Upper bound (my pick): a year.** Up to the start's day 12 months on, clamped (`latestFirstPayment`; 29 Feb 2024 → 28 Feb 2025). It covers 90-day, 6-month and 12-month deferrals and catches a year slip. The calendar dims days outside (day after the start … a year on). Hint: "Pick a first payment no later than {date}, a year after the start date." It is a page rule, not a Review rule. A start + first payment pair carried unchanged from the calculator or a saved loan passes, so an untouched edit never gets stuck.
- **Month end:** only for a first payment on the last day of a month shorter than 31 days, pill chips "On the 28th" / "Last day of each month" (31). The untouched default follows the start's day (31 Jan → Last day); a hand pick defaults to its own day. When the untouched default stands for the 29th/30th (30 Jan → 28 Feb), a third chip "On the 30th" is offered and chosen, so today's stored payment_day 30 is not lost. Carried 29/30 days from a saved loan work the same way.
- `loanReview`: `firstPaymentOn` is now required. 'firstPayment' replaces 'paymentDay' as a missing field (also covers a day the date cannot stand for). A first payment not after the start is `{ reason: 'first-payment' }` (was 'startDate' in the missing list), checked after 'start-after-payoff' because an earlier start mends both. `save.paymentDay` and `scheduleParams.day` are unchanged (null unless the first payment's own day differs).
- **F4 retired:** `firstPaymentOn(start, day)` is gone. Plan line added to `add-loan-plan.md`.
- **Pre-fill:** the calculator's first payment is untouched when it equals the default; otherwise it is set and carries its own day (the calculator sends no `day`, so a 31 Jan → 28 Feb hand-off keeps the 28th, as its schedule had it). Edit shows the saved first payment and payment_day. Untouched edits write back identical terms (pinned for the wireframe, 31st month-end, 30th-on-28-Feb, the Founder's loan, and a >12-month legacy gap), and `choose(…, false)` means no past/upcoming question.

## 2026-10-13 — Dilip — Part 5 platform fixes: Pro identity, TRANSFER webhook, Sentry reports and breadcrumbs, realtime echo, timezone write (DONE, no commits, no deploy)
**Outcome:** done. The likeliest cause of "app says Pro, database says no" is our own code, proven against HEAD. `ensureConfigured` in src/api/pro.ts never calls `logIn` for a second account in the same app run. `configure` is synchronous, so the first sign-in's IIFE ran `configuring = null` before the outer assignment, and the resolved-true promise stayed behind as the answer for every later account. Sign out, then sign in elsewhere without relaunching, and the SDK still spoke and BOUGHT for the first account. That fits c2ad25b3 showing Pro while 95810acb kept getting webhook writes. The TRANSFER gap is also fixed (webhook code only; the Founder deploys).

**What changed (my paths only):**
- `supabase/functions/revenuecat-webhook/index.ts`: TRANSFER handled before the app_user_id check. New Deno-free `transfer.ts` (same pattern as send-push/card.ts) plans it:
  - copies the giver's freshest paid-up row (latest end date, then latest write) to each receiver, unless the receiver already runs as long or longer;
  - switches the giver's rows off (pro=false, will_renew=false), but only rows written before `event_timestamp_ms`, so a delayed retry cannot undo a later purchase;
  - never copies or switches off a `dev.*` script grant (supabase/seed/pro-state-*.sql), since copying one would hand out Pro with no end date;
  - skips non-uuid ids and logs; idempotent on retry.
  Docs: https://www.revenuecat.com/docs/integrations/webhooks/event-types-and-fields#transfer-fields (TRANSFER has only transferred_from/transferred_to, plus store/environment sometimes; it is sent once, for the destination).
- `src/api/pro.ts`, exports unchanged:
  - a per-account configure gate: a call for B while A's sign-in runs waits, then calls logIn(B);
  - `isFor()` ignores CustomerInfo whose `originalAppUserId` is not the signed-in id (listener, getCustomerInfo, restore). Safe because configure has always passed `appUserID`, so there are no anonymous customers;
  - the server copy is read through `rpc('is_pro', { p_user })`, granted to authenticated in 20260831100007 and the same call confirm-pro.ts makes.
- `src/lib/failure.ts`: new `reportFailure(thrown, handled, tags)` and `failureFingerprint()`.
  - Sends ONLY the PostgREST code (tag + extra), and fingerprints [handled, code or error name, message with ids and digits blanked].
  - Sends a clean Error copy (name, message, stack), so `details`/`hint` never leave the phone.
  - The on-screen line and the dev console.log are unchanged.
- `src/providers/query-provider.tsx`: `createQueryClient()`.
  - QueryCache onError → Sentry in Release, `handled: query-read`, `query: <first key segment>` (shape-checked, else 'other');
  - once per query per run, at most 3 per cause, 20 per run.
  - MutationCache onSuccess calls `noteOwnWrite()`. It runs after the server answers and before each mutation's own onSuccess.
- `src/providers/realtime-provider.tsx`: dead `dashboard` keys gone; each key is debounced 400 ms, re-read at least every 1.5 s.
  - An echo within 3 s of our own write skips only queries that started a read or were invalidated after that write landed. Everything else re-reads as before.
  - The skip set is chosen once, before invalidating: invalidateQueries re-asks its predicate after its own invalidate. A test caught that bug.
- `src/api/push.ts`: the launch read now selects `reminders_enabled_at, timezone`, and the timezone is written only when it differs or the read failed. `enableReminders` is unchanged.
- `src/app/_layout.tsx` (Sentry.init block + one import only):
  - `beforeBreadcrumb: scrubBreadcrumb`, `beforeSend: scrubEvent` and `...{ enableNetworkBreadcrumbs: false }`. The RN type does not list that option; RN forwards it (wrapper.js:158) and native reads it (Pods SentyOptionsInternal.m:162).
  - New `src/lib/sentry-breadcrumbs.ts`: fetch/xhr/http keep method, host, path and status; they lose query, fragment, `http.query`/`http.fragment`, and uuids in paths become `<id>`. Navigation loses params and queries.
- Tests:
  - new: src/__tests__/{supabase/revenuecat-transfer, api/pro-identity, api/push-timezone, lib/failure-report, lib/sentry-breadcrumbs, providers/query-provider, providers/realtime-echo};
  - updated: src/api/pro-source{,-sdk}.test.tsx (rpc + originalAppUserId), src/lib/failure.test.ts, src/providers/realtime-provider.test.tsx.

**Rules I decided:**
- Year highlight: the picked month if it is in the year shown; else this month in this year; else none.
- Choose month and Choose year take only exact yyyy-mm-dd dates, between the floor and today.
- Percents are whole, half up, with BigInt. Values over 100 are kept; with no income the result is null.
- `over` is left < 0.
- Spending is money out on receipts, bills and subscriptions. Pay never counts. Payoffs are Bills.
- Bills in retired categories are folded (family → health). Categories: top 6, ties by id. Merchants: top 5, ordered by amount, then times, then name.
- Next due: strictly after today, one row per plan. A plan already paid this month is walked to its next date via `nextDueAfter`. Loans kept out of bills are excluded.
- Habits: the first 3 in the Habits page's order. Saved so far covers every active habit.
- Moved this month: a pot counts in full; removed pots are excluded.
- Coming up: active subscriptions only. The month figure is the year ÷ 12, rounded once on the total.

**Disagrees with the design:**
- Next due: Housing is paid on the 1st, so on 12 Oct the next 2 by date are AEP (22 Oct) and Housing (1 Nov), not Netflix (9 Nov).
- Where it goes: with Q3, Hulu files under its own category, not Other.
- "Subscriptions · 3 $99.99" vs Coming up $115.98/mo: the mock data does not add up.

## 2026-10-13 — Dilip — CEO follow-ups: realtime echo skip per row, Postgres message privacy (DONE, no commits)
- **Echo skip, now per row.** MutationCache onSuccess records the rows a write named: `rowIdsIn(data, variables)`.
  - It takes bare uuids, `id` fields, and the `id` of an object one level in.
  - It never takes ids a write only points at (`card_id`, `accountIds`).
  - A debounced burst skips a query only when EVERY change names a row (`payload.new?.id ?? payload.old?.id`) that we wrote within 3 s, and the query started a read after the latest of those writes landed.
  - Another device's row, a change with no id, or a mixed burst is re-read as normal.
  - Tests pin all of it: another device's row within 3 s IS re-read, and a real mutation through createQueryClient teaches the rows.
  - A mutant that ignores row identity fails exactly those tests.
- **Postgres message privacy.** failure.ts scrubs the message before it reaches Sentry; the same text goes into the exception value, the stack's first line and the fingerprint.
  - Quoted values become `"<value>"`, and `(cols)=(values)` becomes `(cols)=(<value>)`. Column names are kept.

## 2026-10-13 — Diego (second instance) — Idempotent creates, step 1: API layer + salary + source-payment (DONE, no commits; stopped before the batch-1 screens as briefed)
**Outcome:** a create given a client id now files at most one row however often Save is pressed. Salary and source-payment are wired. The other screens wait for batch 1.

**API (`src/api/mutations.ts`, `useCreateHabit` in `src/api/habits.ts`):**
- New `insertOnce(table, values, userId, columns, id?)`, used by `useCreate` and `useCreateHabit`. Both take an optional `id` in the variables (`ClientId`). With no id, it behaves exactly as before.
- `mayHaveWritten(error)`: no non-empty `code` means the write may have landed. postgrest-js answers a dropped fetch with `code: ''` and status 0 (checked in 2.112.3); gateway pages and deadlines carry no code. Any code means PostgREST or Postgres answered and rolled back.
- An id whose last attempt may have landed goes in a module-wide `unanswered` set. The next attempt selects by id first. Found: it updates with the current values and resolves as a create. Not found: it inserts under that id. Success clears the mark; a coded refusal does not set one. The happy path is one request.
- An insert refused with 23505 on `"<table>_pkey"` (a late landing, or a double tap) becomes the same update. RLS hides the key detail, so the constraint name is the signal. Every create table keeps its default pkey name, since none was ever renamed.
- `PaymentValues.from_bank_account_id` is now `string | null`, required.

**Screens:**
- `src/app/source-payment.tsx`: `useState(() => randomUUID())` per visit, sent as `id`. `from_bank_account_id: source || null` instead of leaving the key off, so a retry that finds the first row clears an account no longer chosen. I confirmed the column is live and nullable with one read-only `information_schema` query (`db query --linked`). This reverses the pinned "no key at all" test contract.
- `src/app/salary.tsx`:
  - New pays get a client id the first time a Save tries to file them (`clientIds`, keyed by the page's `salary-N`). `filedIds` is the written-id guard: a filed pay is updated on Save again, never created twice.

## 2026-10-13 — Diego — Part 5 batch 1: confirmPro, past reads await, scan hint (DONE, no commits)
**Outcome:** a Pro write the database refuses while the app shows Pro is now asked about again before any failure line. A save or delete whose past-charges or habit-days read has not answered waits for that read instead of failing. A scan that reads nothing shows a hint, not the failure line.

**New `src/api/confirm-pro.ts`:**
- `confirmPro()` asks in this order:
  1. `is_pro` for the signed-in id;
  2. RevenueCat, past its cache, trusted only when `originalAppUserId` matches the signed-in id;
  3. `is_pro` again, every second, for up to 10 s.
- It answers `'pro'`, `'free'` or `'unknown'`. `'free'` is only given once the published Pro status shows free, so the explainer does not bounce straight back.
- `useProWrite().run(write)` handles a write that hits the wall:
  - a free app gets the explainer, unless the page was already left;
  - a Pro app gets "One moment…" (`pro.confirm.wait`) while it asks, then one retry when the database agrees;
  - otherwise the original error is thrown.
- The client and `react-native-purchases` are required lazily, so the screens' tests load neither.

**Other changes:**
- `src/lib/pro-refusal.ts` also matches "Skip Pro removes the limit" (the free allowance on cards and accounts).
- `load()` added to `useHabitPastDays` (src/api/habits.ts) and `usePastCharges` (src/api/past-charges.ts). It joins a read already in flight and rejects only on a real failure.
  - `choose` and `chooseDelete` take an optional `past` from `load()`.
  - Without it they still return null before the read, so add-bill keeps working.
- Wired into:
  - habit-new, add-receipt, voice-review, add-card and add-account (`useProWrite`);
  - habit-new, add-subscription, bill/[id], subscription/[id], loan/[id] and add-loan (`load()`).

## 2026-10-13 — Diego — Auth: sign-out leaves other phones signed in; same-password message (DONE, no commits)
**Outcome:** both Founder-approved fixes (via Jay) are done and tested.

**1) Sign-out is local (`src/api/auth.ts`):**
- `signOut()` now calls `supabase.auth.signOut({ scope: 'local' })`, after the same steps in the same order: forgetThisDevice, forgetThisPersonsVoice, cancelWrapUpNotification.
- `deleteAccount()` signs out locally too. Its comment: the account's sessions were deleted with its auth.users row, so only this phone's copy is left.
- Checked against auth-js 2.112.3 (installed) and the published docs. `local` POSTs `/logout?scope=local`, so the server ends this session's refresh tokens. Then `_removeSession` fires SIGNED_OUT. It still fires when the request fails or the server answers 401/403/404. Only `others` skips it.
- What the app does on SIGNED_OUT: there is no explicit cache clear. SessionProvider sets the session to null. Every user query is keyed `[key, userId]` and `enabled: Boolean(userId)`, and the realtime channel drops with `userId`. Settings navigates with `resetTo('/welcome')` after `signOut()` resolves. There is no query persister.

**2) Same password (`readable()`):**
- GoTrue answers 422 with code `same_password` and the words "New password should be different from the old password." Older API versions send `error_code`; auth-js maps both to `error.code`.
- The check runs before the short-password check: by code first, then by the words "different from the old password".
- The new key `api.auth.samePassword` is in **`src/i18n/messages/api.ts`, not `messages/auth.ts`**. `messages.test.ts` requires each key to start with its area's name, and all `api.auth.*` keys live in api.ts. api.ts was clean in git before the edit.
- en uses the app's curly apostrophe ("That’s"). 91 English lines use it, 3 use a straight one.
- `src/app/reset-password.tsx` (the only `updatePassword` caller) shows the error under the confirm field.

**Tests (`src/api/auth.test.ts`, 42, 11 new):**
- signOut passes `{ scope: 'local' }`, in the order forget, voice, stores, searches, wrapUp, signOut.
- deleteAccount's sign-out is local.
- Real supabase-js client with a fake server, run through the app's own `signOut`/`deleteAccount`/`updatePassword`:
  - Sign-out sends one `POST …/logout?scope=local`, then SIGNED_OUT, with the stored session gone. This also holds offline (FAILURE_MESSAGE comes back) and when the server says 403 user_not_found after a delete.
  - A same_password refusal reaches the new line in both server shapes, and weak_password still gets the short-password line.
- Wording: by code, by words, code with short-sounding words, genuinely short, unknown → FAILURE_MESSAGE, es/fr.
- Mutants on scratch copies via a scratch jest config, with the real files checked unchanged by md5: 10/10 killed, and the control passed.

**Gates:**
- jest: auth + settings, settings-languages, verify-otp, auth-languages, sign-in-handoff, what-skip-can-do, oauth + src/i18n = 17 suites, 185/185.
- eslint (cache cleared, --no-cache, --max-warnings 0) and prettier: clean on my 3 files.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p .`: 4–5 errors, all `refreshFailed` in payments tests, from another session's in-flight `src/lib/query-state.ts` work (written 14:59). None are in my files.
- Full `npx jest`: 9625/9651. On rerunning the 18 failing suites alone, 9 pass. What remains is 5 s timeouts on a loaded machine, the 20 ms parser speed test at 21 ms, another session's new home-refetch-error test, and the Ask Sam prepared library (another session is editing the knowledge files).

**Worth knowing:**
- An offline sign-out clears the phone but leaves that one server session alive. Nothing on the phone can reach it any more. Global had the same gap.
- Under global, other phones were signed out but kept their device_tokens rows, so they could still get this account's pushes. Local ends that mismatch.
- No `Purchases.logOut` on sign-out (`src/api/pro.ts`, not mine). This is unchanged by this work.

## 2026-10-13 — Diego — Item 33 data side: a failed background refresh keeps the last figures (`refreshFailed`) (DONE, no commits)
**Outcome:** `usePayments`, `usePlanMonth` and `usePaymentLabels` now follow one rule.
- `isError` is true only when a required read failed with nothing to show.
- The new `refreshFailed` is true when any read's latest attempt failed but every required read still holds data.
- On a failed refresh the figures stay the very same objects, so the memo does not walk again. No screen was touched; Dana wires the shared note when it exists.

**TanStack 5.102.2, checked in the installed source:**
- `createResult` gives `isLoadingError = isError && data === undefined` and `isRefetchError = isError && data !== undefined`.
- The error reducer leaves `data` alone.
- A retry over data keeps `status: 'error'` until it succeeds, so `refreshFailed` stays on until a refresh works.
- The rule is written with `isError` and `data`, the same definitions. Other suites' fake queries carry only `data`/`isLoading`/`isError`/`refetch`, so they keep working unchanged.

**New return types:**
- `usePaymentLabels(): { sources; labelOf; isLoading; isError; refreshFailed: boolean; refetch }`
- `PaymentsData = { payments; listFloor; free; labelOf; sources; isLoading; isError; refreshFailed: boolean; refetch }`
- `PlanMonthData = { view; hasPlans; labelOf; isLoading; isError; refreshFailed: boolean; refetch }`

**Required reads:** bills, subscriptions, charges, payoffs, cards and accounts. For the ledger hooks, the names (cards + accounts) count as one read, in once neither is loading or failed with nothing to show. The rule's 6 lines are written in both files because several suites replace `@/api/payment-labels` whole, so `payment-ledger.ts` can import only `usePaymentLabels` from it.

**Tests:**
- `payment-ledger.test.tsx` (74): a first load that fails gives `isError` and no `refreshFailed`.
- For each of the 6 reads on its own:
  - a load that works, then a refresh that fails, gives `refreshFailed` with `isError` false;
  - the same `payments`/`view` objects come back, with 0 walks;
  - a later refresh that works clears both.
- A new charge still shows while bills fail to refresh.
- No `refreshFailed` while another read is still on its first load.
- `payment-labels.test.tsx` (12): the same for cards and accounts.

Needs migration `20261013700001_spend_goal.sql` applied live before "Add receipt" works (until then it shows the failure line; "Just remove it" works as before).

**Cause:** "I spent it" closes the goal and keeps its moves, so its money stays out of savings. A receipt added for the same purchase then counted as that month's spending, so the 1st's wrap-up moved that much less into savings: savings lost it twice. Without the receipt, Current balance and Insights never saw the purchase at all.

**Design:**
- New `spend_goal(p_id, p_receipt, p_merchant, p_purchased_on, p_card_id, p_bank_account_id, p_book_id) → uuid` (security definer, savings lock, `for update` on the open goal): inserts the receipt for `goal_saved(p_id)` (start amount + moves; the client sends no amount), closes the goal and sets new `goals.receipt_id` (FK to receipts, on delete set null, unique). Replays by receipt id. Refuses 42501 / 22023 / 23514 (someone else's card or account; book via receipts_own_book) / P0002 in delete_goal's words ('gone').
- Savings maths (`src/lib/savings.ts`): `paidFromGoals(purchases, moves)` = max(0, start_amount + Σ moves) per linked receipt; `savingsFlows(entries, paidByGoals)` counts a goal's receipt only for max(0, |receipt| − paid). Used by "so far" and by the month close/update (`closingFlows`). The receipt counts in full in the money book, Current balance and Insights.
- New `src/api/goal-purchases.ts` (reads goals.receipt_id, paged; a DB without the column reads as none). `savings.ts` only imports and calls it.
- Page `src/app/goal-spent.tsx` (`?id=`): lead, goal card with the fixed amount, Store (goal name), Date (Today/Yesterday/Pick date), Paid with (tiles + Skip), footer "Add receipt" + "Just remove it". Toasts `toast.goal.spent` (check) / `toast.goal.deleted` ('deleted'). Default receipt book, else General.
- `save-goal.tsx`: the 'spent' choice pushes `/goal-spent`; put-back is unchanged.

**Tests:** new goal-spent-money (13, hand-checked fixture across savingsSummary/monthTotals/moneyBook/heroFigures/spendSummary/goalsSummary), goal-spent screen (15), spend-goal-migration static (7); goals API +2, savings hooks +4, savings close +4, goals-screens updated +1. SQL: `supabase/checks/spend_goal.sql` 37 checks PASS on an isolated local DB (project SkipBudgetDrewChecks, ports 555xx, all migrations; stopped, volumes removed); savings_goals.sql 150, receipt_books, free_capture_allowance, habits, habit_past_days, update_habit_and_days all PASS with it; re-applying the migration is clean; delete_my_account still removes everything; 4/4 SQL mutants caught.

**Gates:** tsc: 0 errors in my files (7 elsewhere, other sessions' payments/salary tests). eslint (cache cleared, --no-cache, --max-warnings 0) and prettier clean on all 15 TS files. jest: 42 suites / 857 tests (goal, savings, insights, money-book, i18n, guards) pass.

## 2026-10-13 — Drew — Stopped habits keep their days in "Saved so far" (PARTIAL: maths + View details done; Habits page wiring BLOCKED on src/api/habits.ts; no commits)
**Outcome:** the rule is in the maths and pinned to the cent. The Habits page hero can't count stopped habits yet, because the page never reads them: `useHabits()` filters `.is('archived_at', null)`, and no other habit read exists. A drafted, mirror-verified patch for the wiring is in scratch, NOT applied.

**Why stopping drops the days:** not `savedAllTime`, and not the taps (`useHabitTaps` reads every habit receipt, stopped ones included, and `useHabitDays` filters nothing). The habit list is the cause: `useHabits()` returns active habits only → `active` → `maths` → `savedAllTime(maths, …)` sums only the habits it is given. Insights has the same hole (`habitsSummary` gets `useHabits().data`).

**Rule (doc comment at the top of src/lib/habit-week.ts):**
- Saved = skipped days x price, summed in cents.
- A skipped day is a saving day with no receipt for the habit dated on it; two receipts on one day count as one bought day.
- Saving days run from countsFrom (the creation day) to the last saving day. For a running habit that is yesterday. For a stopped habit it is the day before `stoppedOn`, or yesterday if that is earlier.
- The stop day never saves (it was not over while the habit ran), and no later day does. So stopping leaves Saved exactly where it stood and it never grows after.
- Price: the stored price. The app refuses to edit an archived habit, so it is the price the habit had when it stopped. The server does not refuse such an edit.
- A habit removed with everything is in no list and has no receipts, so it adds nothing.

**Files (mine only):**
- `src/lib/habit-week.ts`:
  - `HabitMaths.stoppedOn?: string | null`.
  - New `stoppedOnDay(archivedAt)`: the device-local day of `archived_at`. A bare yyyy-mm-dd is taken as is; anything else that is not a timestamp throws RangeError.
  - Internal `lastSavingDay` used by `skippedDaysInWeek` and `skippedDaysAllTime`, and so by `savedInWeek`, `savedAllTime` and habitHistory's `saved`.
  - habitHistory lists no skipped day from the stop day on, and no 'today', for a stopped habit.
  - limit, progress, dayState and the weeks habitHistory lists are unchanged; a stopped habit has no card.
  - Running habits: identical results.
- `src/app/habit/[id].tsx`: Saved = `savedAllTime([maths], own, today)`, the same function as the hero. It was `fromCents(skipped * toCents(price))`, which gives the same figure for running habits.
- `src/lib/habit-week.test.ts`: +18 tests. Stopped counted to the day before the stop and frozen for years; Saved unmoved on the stop day; receipts on or after the stop are spent, never saved; weekly $25 / $10 / $0; mixed with a running habit, $145.80 = 14580 cents; Keep past days $80 vs Remove everything $45 (and stale receipts of a removed habit add nothing); stop on the creation day or before it = 0; a null stop = running; a 5-price x 5-stop freeze property; history rows sum to 3500 cents; no today once stopped; a bad stop throws; `stoppedOnDay` checks built from local times, so they hold in any TZ.
- `src/__tests__/habits/habits-saved-parity.test.tsx` (new, 10 tests): the real Habits page and the real View details on the same reads, 8 days, 5–12 Oct. Hero = the habits' own pages added up, to the cent. Hand-counted on Fri 9 Oct: $5.00, $225.00, $16.00, $82.25, hero $328.25. A stopped habit: $161.20 from the stop day on, $489.45 together with the running habits (pure check until wired).

The 4 failures are `home-refetch-error.test.tsx`, another session's in-flight file about Home's "Couldn't refresh" note; Home does not import habit-week.

## 2026-10-13 — Diego — RevenueCat at sign-out: Pro no longer lingers; logOut NOT added (PARTIAL by decision, no commits)
**Outcome:** the Pro state no longer lingers after sign-out. I did NOT add `Purchases.logOut()`: RevenueCat's own rules for this app's id model say never to call it, and it would break `pro.ts`'s identity check. Needs a CEO/Jay call if logOut is still wanted.

**Why no logOut (sources: RevenueCat "Identifying customers" docs; react-native-purchases 10.8.1 installed):**
- logOut makes an anonymous `$RCAnonymousID`. For apps that use only their own ids, the docs say: "Only configure the SDK with a custom App User ID, and never call .logout()".
- After a logOut, logIn to an account RevenueCat has never seen merges it with the anonymous id, and "original_app_user_id will be the anonymous id".
  - `isFor()` (and `storeSaysPro` in confirm-pro.ts) trust only `originalAppUserId === userId`. For that account the SDK answer would never count again, on any phone: a purchase is not seen until the webhook lands, and `restore()` says false.
  - Deleting your account and signing up again on the same phone hits this.
- The docs also warn that "a provided user's subscription may be transferred to an anonymous ID - which can only be brought back through a restore". A renewal seen on the signed-out screen could move it. The webhook skips anonymous receivers, so the account would quietly lapse at its next renewal.
- The next account cannot inherit Pro without logOut. Every SDK read waits behind the serialised logIn, and `isFor` drops another id's late answer. Two new tests prove this.

**What changed (`src/api/pro.ts`, `useProSource`):**
- The remembered SDK answer is dropped at sign-out (render-phase `setSdk(null)` when `userId` is null).
- An effect removes cached `['entitlement', <user>]` answers when `userId` goes null. The signed-out key is kept.
- One comment explains why RevenueCat is left signed in until the next sign-in's logIn.
- Before the fix (same tests on the old pro.ts): the signed-out account's `entitlement` answer stayed cached. The same account signing back in after its Pro ended was shown `{ pro: true, ready: true }` until the reads came back.

**Tests (`src/__tests__/api/pro-identity.test.tsx`, 11, 5 new):**
- The mock gains logOut, isAnonymous, a server gate and an ordered log of SDK calls. The new tests use one QueryClient per test with `gcTime: Infinity`.
- Nothing says Pro after sign-out: published `{false,false}`, cache entry gone, no listener left.
- The same account back waits for its answer afresh and never shows Pro.
- A → sign-out → B: the SDK calls are exactly `logIn:B`, then `read:B`. It ends as B, and B is never shown Pro.
- Sign-out never calls logOut and never leaves RevenueCat on an anonymous id.
- A signed-in account's server answer is refetched by a purchase's invalidation.
- Mutants via scratch config + moduleNameMapper, with the real files checked unchanged by md5. Killed: no SDK reset, no cache drop, logOut at sign-out. Control passed.
  - Survivor: dropping the `if (userId) return` guard. It removes the live query once at sign-in, and useQuery rebuilds it on the next render, so the only effect is an extra fetch. Not pinned.

**Gates:**
- jest `src/api` + `src/__tests__/api`: 64 suites, 1158/1158.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p .`: 0, whole tree.
- eslint (cache cleared, --no-cache, --max-warnings 0) and prettier: clean on both files.
- Full `npx jest`: 10076/10097. 5 suites failed. 4 of them pass alone: receipt-detail and habit-receipt-rows are other sessions' in-flight edits, plus the two i18n suites under load. The Ask Sam prepared library is stale from another session's knowledge edits.

**Open:**
- If a shared Apple ID moving Pro between Skip accounts is the worry, the lever is RevenueCat's dashboard Restore Behavior ("Transfer" vs "Keep with original App User ID"). logOut is not that lever. Founder/CEO decision.
- #32 follow-up after Dmitri's GO (same day):
  - `cards.tsx`: `savingsUnread = savings.isError && !savings.refreshFailed`, and the same for `goalsUnread`. The Goals tile now checks unread BEFORE the active count. Before this, a moves read that failed with nothing cached showed savings as held − 0 and could count a reached goal as active.
  - `home.tsx`: the note shows only with `&& !balance.isError`, so it never sits beside the balance failure line.
  - Tests: cards-refetch-error gains "shows no Savings/Goals figure, only Open"; home's mixed case now expects no note. All three fail on the old logic (scratch copy).
  - Gates: home/cards refetch suites and cards.test 50/50; eslint and prettier clean; tsc's 2 errors are in `transactions.test.tsx` (another session's in-flight `transactions.tsx`), not mine.

## 2026-10-13 — Diego — Founder fixes 3a (data) and 4: deleting recorded pay; the free scan count stays spent (DONE, no commits; migrations NOT applied live)
**For Dana: hooks and types (`src/api/pay.ts`):**
- `useDeletePay(): { countPast(id: string, today: string): Promise<number>; remove(input: PayDeleteInput): Promise<{ id: string; choice: PastDelete }>; removing: boolean }`
- `type PayDeleteInput = { id: string /* salary_sources row */; choice: PastDelete /* 'keep' | 'everything' */; today: string /* useToday */ }`
- `countPast` = paydays on the record + paydays due by today not written down yet (what the ledger already shows). It rejects on a failed read. 0 means nothing is in history, so the plain confirm is safe.
- `remove` with 'everything' on a pay already gone (P0002) resolves, so a retried Save is safe.

**3a: what I found.**
- A pay's paydays are `pay_received` rows, with `salary_source_id` set to null on delete. Removing a salary already kept its pay, but only what the sweep had written. Paydays due and not yet written were only projected from the salary, so they vanished with it.
- Savings months are frozen pots (`close_my_savings_month`). Open months, "so far" and every balance come from the same ledger, which reads `pay_received` plus the projection.

**3a: what changed.**
- 'keep': writes this pay's due paydays first (`recordDuePayOf`; fails loudly, and on a 23505 from a racing sweep it reads again once), then deletes the salary. Two requests: if the delete fails, what was written is exactly what the sweep would have written.
- 'everything': `delete_salary_and_pay(p_salary)`, which runs as the caller. It locks the salary FOR UPDATE, deletes its paydays, then the salary; otherwise P0002 'there is no such pay'. Revoked from public and anon, granted to authenticated.
- `recordDuePay` now shares `readDuePay` and `duePay` (src/lib/pay-record.ts) with the keep path; its behaviour is unchanged (pay.test 70/70).

**3a: proof.**

  - Keep: Current balance, Checking, Card and all five months are equal to the cent; no closed pot offers an update; nothing of Acme is projected after today, and the next sweep writes none.
  - Control: deleting without writing 9 Oct first drops the balance by 1,834.62.
  - Everything: balance, income and Checking drop by exactly 18,256.96. Months drop by 3,580.00 / 5,503.86 / 3,669.24 / 3,669.24 / 1,834.62; closed pots offer earnedChange −3580 / −5503.86 / −3669.24 / −3669.24.

**4: what I found.**

- A reading of nothing still filed as 'scan': `applyScan` always set the capture source.

**4: what changed.**
- `capture_usage` table: one row per receipt read by camera or upload, written by an AFTER INSERT trigger. It copies the receipt's created_at, which the server stamps for free accounts. `receipt_id` is ON DELETE SET NULL.
- Row level security: the owner may only read; insert, update and delete are revoked from the API, and anon has nothing.
- `enforce_scan_is_pro` now counts usage rows; otherwise it is unchanged.
- Back-fill from existing receipts, re-run safe through a unique index on receipt_id. Pro scans are recorded too, as they were counted before, so a lapse within the month still counts them.
- App: `useCaptureUsage` reads usage from local midnight on the 1st, keyed by month, and falls back to receipts with no table. Receipt writes and realtime receipt changes refresh it. A reading of nothing files as 'manual'.

## 2026-10-13 — Diego — The sweep runs when the day turns while the app stays open (DONE, no commits)
**Outcome:** while Home is mounted, a timer to the next local midnight (plus 1 s) runs the same sweep the launch and resume path runs, once per turn of the day, then re-arms. It is cleared on unmount and on sign-out (the effect re-runs on `userId`). A resume at the same moment does not run it twice.

**What changed:**
- `src/api/refresh.ts`, only the `useKeepSchedulesCurrent` region (lines 177-241; line 44 untouched):
  - New `MIDNIGHT_GRACE_MS` and exported `msUntilNextMidnight(now)`, which handles 23/25-hour clock-change days.
  - The resume guard is now day-aware. A return within 60 s still skips, unless the day has turned since the last sweep; before, a 23:59:30 sweep would have swallowed a 00:00:00 resume.
  - The midnight timer runs only if no sweep has covered the new day yet. That makes it exactly once per flip, and a late-firing timer after a resume does nothing.
- `src/lib/use-today.ts` untouched: it re-checks every 60 s and on resume, not at midnight, so it is not a day-flip signal.
- Overlapping sweeps across midnight cannot double-file: the recorders upsert with `ignoreDuplicates`.
- New `src/__tests__/api/refresh-midnight.test.tsx` (14):
  - no run before midnight;
  - one run for the new day at 00:00:01, invalidating `['charges']`, then re-arming for the next day;
  - a resume 0.5 s past midnight, inside the 60 s window, sweeps the new day and the timer then does not;
  - a resume after the timer does not double-run;
  - the timer stops at unmount and at sign-out;
  - `msUntilNextMidnight` lands exactly on local midnight across month/year ends and the North American and European clock-change days.
- Scratch-copy mutants (time-only guard, unconditional timer sweep, no clearTimeout, no re-arm, no timer) are all caught.

## 2026-10-13 — Drew — Next due inside a charged cycle: findings, then the form-hint helper `effectiveNextDue` (DONE, 2 new files, no commits)
**Findings (read-only, earlier today):** see `.claude/team/dev/next-due-floor-report.md`. Cause: a running plan's stored next date can sit before its own floor (starts_on / started_on). Readers that walk the schedule are right; the bill and subscription pages, the reminders page, the forms and the server's `reminders_due` print the stored column. Agreed fix: the SQL floor trigger plus a one-off update, in the month-end session's migration series.

**Built:** `src/lib/next-due-hint.ts` (new) and `src/__tests__/payments/next-due-hint.test.ts` (new). card-ledger.ts, charges.ts, bill-month.ts and month-step.ts are imported only.
- `effectiveNextDue({ picked, recurrence, anchorDay?, lastChargedOn, today })` returns `{ next, paidCycle: { start, label: 'week'|'month'|'quarter'|'year', current } | null }`.
  - How it works: the floor comes from `floorAfterCharges`, as Save writes it. The next date is the first `occurrencesInRange` date on or after the floor, with the anchor day. The cycle comes from `cycleStart`.
  - `paidCycle` is non-null exactly when the date moves. It names the newest charged cycle, so a pick in an earlier month says why it lands later.
  - `current` is the only use of `today`.
  - Period: no special case. It goes through the same floor, walk and cycle (label 'month'). Today it never moves, so it never hints. Its fixtures follow the announced monthly-walk contract and switch on by themselves once `occurrencesInRange` walks a period monthly (`PERIODS_WALK`).
  - The look-ahead is 12 months against the trigger's 5 years. The first date on or after a cycle start always falls inside that cycle, so the results are the same.
- **Parity table:** `NEXT_DUE_FLOOR_TABLE` is exported from the test file as plain text, with 33 hand-worked rows: 27 repeating, 6 period. Its line format is `picked anchor recurrence last-charged | floor next paid-start`. The SQL check copies it between `$nextdue$` markers.
- **Tests:** 20 in total; on today's main 16 pass and 4 are period-gated.
  - Every row is checked against the helper, the real `buildBillValues` (next_due_on = picked, starts_on = floor), the real `buildSubscriptionValues` (countsFrom null, earlier and same), the trigger rule worked with `nextOccurrenceFrom`, and `nextDueAfter`.
  - Named cases: the Founder's 15 Nov; a 31st landing on 30 Nov and then 31 Dec only with anchor 31; invalid anchors; a past uncharged date; last month paid; the charge day; labels and `current`; never charged.
  - A hand-counted brute force covers 62,062 cases, 40,229 of them hinted.

**Gap found (needs a decision):** under the period contract, `buildBillValues` still saves a period's starts_on as the picked date (`entry-values.ts`, `starts_on: isPeriod ? start : floorAfterCharges(...)`). The trigger reads starts_on as the floor, so a period's date would never move and set periods keep the original bug. The mirror simulation proves it: with the contract applied, "floors a set period as the bill form saves it" fails (15 Oct vs 1 Nov). With the period save floored too, all 19 pass. Either the save floors periods as well, or the trigger floors by charges.

**Gates:**
- jest, my suite plus charges, entry-values, bill-month, month-end/*, month-end-parity and the no-route guard: 13 suites, 275 passed, 4 skipped.
- My suite also passes in Pacific/Auckland, America/Los_Angeles and Asia/Kolkata.
- tsc on the whole tree: 0. eslint (cache cleared, --no-cache, --max-warnings 0) and prettier: clean on both files.
- Mutants on a scratch mirror (`scratchpad/drew-nextdue/mirror`; the real files' md5 is unchanged):
  - 10/10 killed on main's contract;
  - 3/3 period mutants killed under the simulated period contract;
  - the no-op control survived both times.
- `rules.md` was not found anywhere; I followed the log's usual gates.

## 2026-10-13 — Diego — Flaky labels test fixed (test-only, no commits)
- **Cause:** `payment-labels.test.tsx` held every read in one queue and released it in order (`mockHeld.shift()`). The cards and accounts reads are not always queued in the same order, so 9 runs in 20 released the accounts first, and `isLoading` was already false at the assertion.
